question.worked_solution:
The period of $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is $2\pi .$ Therefore, for an integer $n$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+2n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=-1$ into the right-hand-side gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3},$ then $\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-2\pi )=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}.$

Finally, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-2\pi )-2 & =\sqrt{5}(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3})-2 \\  & =\frac{{(\sqrt{5})}^{2}}{3}-2 \\  & =\frac{5}{3}-2 \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
